phase: DB-5 Phase A11 (QCH Query Engine Phase 1.5) + QCH Phase 2A NL planner grounding audit + QCH Phase 2D.1 version identity audit + QCH Phase 2D.4 entity lookup/describe + QCH Phase 2D.6 contributor provenance + QCH Phase 2D.5 submission-level official evaluation
changelog: 0.7.0 (Phase 2D.6 contributor provenance): added ONE primitive operator, 'list_contributors' (contributor ACCOUNTS -- platform provenance identities, never persons -- all, one resolved by handle, or the contributors of one version/submission), a 'contributor' param on list_submissions (a contributor's submissions) and on describe_entity, the list_submissions record fields contributor.submitter / contributor.declared_coauthors, and 'contributor_fields' (list_contributors record fields). Contributor references are resolved DETERMINISTICALLY by QCH (exact/case-insensitive handle, proven former handle, stable account key); an unresolvable reference -- e.g. a person's name -- is UNKNOWN_ENTITY, never a guess and never 'zero submissions'. See docs/QCH_CONTRIBUTOR_PROVENANCE_PHASE2D6.md.

0.6.0 (Phase 2D.5 submission-level official evaluation): added three SUBMISSION-scoped metrics (evaluation.peak_qubits, evaluation.avg_executed_toffoli, evaluation.score) imported from content-addressed snapshots of the official ECDSA.Fail platform API, one primitive operator (list_submissions), a submission_fields list, and submission scope for get_metric/compare_versions when they request evaluation.*/platform.* names. New metrics declare explicit nl_grounding (concept + qualifiers, requires_qualifier) so bare 'score'/'Toffoli'/'qubits' keep their previous grounding. No existing metric, operator or relation was renamed or removed. See docs/QCH_SUBMISSION_EVALUATION_PHASE2D5.md.

0.5.0 (Phase 2D.4 entity lookup/describe): added ONE compound operator, 'describe_entity', so a direct entity question ('tell me about X', 'find version X', 'does X exist?') is answered by describing the entity instead of an arbitrary single-metric lookup that fails as MISSING_DATA when that metric is absent. No metric, relation type, or field was added or renamed. See docs/QCH_ENTITY_LOOKUP_DESCRIBE_PHASE2D4.md.

0.3.0 (Phase 2A audit): corrected 'qubit_count'/'operation_count'/'classical_bit_count' entries -- the code's alias table does NOT resolve these from computed structural analysis (verified by reading qch/query/metrics.py's _ALIASES table); added standalone 'structural.qubit_count'/'structural.operation_count'/'structural.classical_bit_count' entries, which were previously only implied, not documented.

0.4.0 (Phase 2D.1 version identity audit): 'version_metadata_fields' existed in this file already (matching qch.nl.validator's internal _VERSION_METADATA_FIELDS acceptance set) but was never parsed into qch.nl.schema_context.SchemaContext nor rendered into the LLM prompt, so the planner was never told 'external_version_key' is a legal, generic lookup field for filter/get_metric/sort conditions -- this contributed to a 'V5-only' identity-display bug (the milestone label was shown instead of the real canonical key) and to false UNKNOWN_ENTITY responses for real, non-milestone version identifiers. No new field, operator, or metric was added here; this is a documentation/wiring fix exposing data this file already had. See docs/QCH_VERSION_IDENTITY_PHASE2D1.md.
purpose: The contract between a future NL query planner (LLM, not yet integrated) and qch.query.QCHQueryExecutor. A planner may ONLY emit plans built from the operators/params/metrics/relations listed here -- it never invents a metric name, operator, or relation_type not present in this file. This file is generated by hand from the current qch.query.operators.OPERATORS registry and qch.history data; regenerate it whenever an operator or metric is added.

answerability_statuses.name: answerable
answerability_statuses.meaning: the plan executed and produced a complete, trustworthy result

answerability_statuses.name: partially_answerable
answerability_statuses.meaning: some but not all requested fields/metrics were available; see missing_fields

answerability_statuses.name: missing_data
answerability_statuses.meaning: the plan is well-formed but the referenced version/metric/circuit does not exist or has no data

answerability_statuses.name: unsupported_operation
answerability_statuses.meaning: the plan names an operator not in this schema

answerability_statuses.name: ambiguous
answerability_statuses.meaning: the plan under-specifies which logical circuit to use and more than one exists

answerability_statuses.name: invalid_plan
answerability_statuses.meaning: the plan is syntactically malformed (missing/wrong-typed required params) -- never reaches semantic evaluation

operators.name: list_versions
operators.returns: list of version records (identity fields + every available metric merged in)
operators.description: Every CircuitVersion of the resolved logical circuit.

operators.name: filter
operators.returns: list, subset of the input list
operators.description: Keeps records satisfying every condition (AND). A record missing a referenced metric is excluded, not treated as failing.

operators.name: sort
operators.description: Records missing the sort field always sort last, regardless of order.

operators.name: list_transitions
operators.returns: list of transition records (parent/child identity + historical_time; metric_before/after/absolute_change/percentage_change if 'metric' given)
operators.description: Every TransformationEdge of the given relation_type. If 'metric' is given, a transition is included only when that metric is available on BOTH endpoints.

operators.name: compute_delta
operators.description: Annotates transition-like records with one metric's delta. Call multiple times (once per metric) to compare several metrics on the same transitions -- this is how multi-metric composed queries are built, never a dedicated per-combination operator.

operators.name: traverse
operators.returns: list of version records reachable in the given direction
operators.description: predecessors/successors are single-hop; ancestors/descendants walk transitively (bounded by max_hops if given). Always specify relation_type when the graph has more than one edge type between the same versions (see relation_types).

operators.name: group_by

key.note: a field name, optionally '<field>:year' or '<field>:year_month' to bucket an ISO-8601 timestamp field

operators.description: Buckets records by key and aggregates one metric per bucket.

operators.name: get_metric
operators.description: Resolves a version by version_id/external_version_key/version_label and returns one metric's value. For a SUBMISSION-scoped metric (evaluation.*, platform.*) it returns that official evaluation fact of the submission the identifier names -- also for a submission with no CircuitVersion (pass the identifier as the question gives it).

operators.name: compare_versions

metrics.note: defaults to the union of every metric known for either version

operators.description: Compares two versions across one or more metrics. When `metrics` includes evaluation.*/platform.* names, those are compared between the two entities' SUBMISSIONS (either side may be a submission with no CircuitVersion).

operators.name: filter_versions
operators.description: list_versions + filter, with an explicit count of versions excluded for lacking a required metric.

operators.name: rank_transitions
operators.description: list_transitions + sort + limit, internally, with an explicit note when fewer transitions were available than requested.

operators.name: describe_entity

version.note: the version (or submission) identifier exactly as the question gives it, or its known external_version_key

submission.note: an exact submission external key; normally not needed -- use 'version' with the question's identifier

contributor.note: a contributor handle exactly as written in the question

operators.returns: an entity description: identity, status, timestamps, every AVAILABLE metric (possibly none), relationship summaries, provenance, and what is unavailable
operators.description: Describes ONE specific entity the question names directly -- use for 'tell me about X', 'describe X', 'find version X', 'show me X', 'what do you know about X', 'does X exist?'. Do NOT use it when the question asks for a specific metric of X (use get_metric), compares X with another version (use compare_versions), asks what branched from / what X branched from (use traverse), or asks for versions satisfying a condition or ranking (use filter_versions/sort/rank_transitions).

operators.name: list_submissions

platform_status.note: the official platform status -- a different vocabulary from lifecycle_status

contributor.note: only this contributor's submissions (a handle exactly as written in the question)

operators.returns: list of submission records: submission_uuid, lifecycle_status, external_version_key (null if the submission has no CircuitVersion), has_official_evaluation, contributor.submitter, and every available evaluation.*/platform.* field
operators.description: Every QCH Submission with its latest official platform evaluation. Use (with filter/sort/limit) for questions about SUBMISSIONS or official evaluation values across submissions, e.g. 'which submissions have official peak qubits below 900', 'which rejected submissions have official evaluation metrics'. Not for CircuitVersion-only metrics such as structural.*.

operators.name: list_contributors

contributor.note: a contributor handle exactly as written in the question; QCH resolves it deterministically

version.note: a version or submission identifier exactly as the question gives it

operators.returns: list of contributor records (see contributor_fields); with 'version', one record per contribution: role SUBMITTER (official owner) or COAUTHOR (declared), current_handle, evidence_class, attribution_path
operators.description: Contributor ACCOUNTS (not persons). contributor=<handle>: that account; version=<id>: who submitted it; neither: all accounts (with filter/sort/limit). For a contributor's submissions use list_submissions with contributor.

relation_types.name: historical_successor
relation_types.meaning: Curated milestone succession. ONLY the 4 edges among the 5 frozen ECDSA.Fail V1-V5 benchmark milestones (a hand-picked subsequence, not every promoted commit in between).

relation_types.name: next_promoted_commit
relation_types.meaning: The COMPLETE, dense chronological chain of all 520 promoted ECDSA.Fail versions (every submission whose Accept/Validate event reached `main`), ordered by position in `git log main`. Deliberately a different relation_type from historical_successor (V1's true next commit is NOT V2).
relation_types.source: COMPUTED (qch.history.version_graph.build_version_graph, DB-5 Phase A11); see that module's docstring for the empirical finding that required this distinction

relation_types.name: branched_from
relation_types.meaning: Links a VALIDATED-but-never-promoted version to the nearest promoted version at or before its real Git fork point (git merge-base). Represents a fork that never rejoined the main lineage -- never conflated with succession.

metrics.definition: Average EXECUTED Toffoli-gate count over 9,024 Fiat-Shamir-derived simulation shots of the official ECDSA.Fail benchmark harness (eval_circuit). Lower is better.
metrics.unit: count (gates, averaged over shots -- may be fractional)
metrics.availability: Only the 5 frozen V1-V5 milestones. Reproducing this for other versions requires running eval_circuit's full shot-based simulation per version, not attempted at scale in Phase 1.5 (real local timing evidence suggested 30s-20+min per run).
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have this metric (all currently V1-V5).

metrics.definition: STATIC count of ccx+ccz operations literally present in the built circuit's operation list -- an upper bound on executed Toffoli count, since some operations may sit behind classical conditions (push_condition/pop_condition) not taken on every shot.
metrics.source: COMPUTED (qch.history.extraction, from a materialized ops.bin artifact via qch.canonical.ecdsafail_ops.ECDSAOpsStructuralParser)
metrics.availability: Any version whose artifact materializes AND uses the post-2026-06-22 zstd-framed 'QECCOPSZ' ops.bin wire format.
metrics.NOT_an_alias_of: toffoli_count -- confirmed by direct comparison on V4/V5: structural=1,403,192/945,508 vs benchmark(executed avg)=1,320,763/903,434 -- close but genuinely different quantities. Likewise NOT an alias of evaluation.avg_executed_toffoli (the official average EXECUTED count): on all 25 comparable versions the static count is 5.2-6.3% higher.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have this metric.

metrics.definition: Peak number of live qubits used by the circuit, computed the same way as the 'qubit_count' alias's stored value (max qubit index + 1) but via structural analysis of a materialized artifact rather than read from a manifest.
metrics.availability: Any version successfully materialized AND structurally analyzed (781-version history: 50 versions as of Phase 1.7).
metrics.NOT_an_alias_of: qubit_count -- the query engine's generic 'qubit_count' alias does NOT read this metric name (see that entry's CORRECTION note); this is a value only reachable by its own literal name. Independently verified numerically IDENTICAL to 'qubit_count' for every version where both happen to exist (V4, V5) -- same real-world quantity, different code path, not unified in the query layer.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have this metric.

metrics.definition: Total number of operations (all kinds) in the built circuit, from structural analysis of a materialized artifact.
metrics.availability: Any version successfully materialized AND structurally analyzed.
metrics.NOT_an_alias_of: operation_count -- same defect as structural.qubit_count vs. qubit_count above.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have this metric.

metrics.definition: Peak number of classical bits used (max classical-bit index + 1), from structural analysis of a materialized artifact.
metrics.availability: Any version successfully materialized AND structurally analyzed.
metrics.NOT_an_alias_of: classical_bit_count -- which is not a real queryable name at all (see that entry); the raw STORED equivalent is 'classical_bits'.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have this metric -- a large change reflects a real algorithmic difference, not noise (see V4 vs V5's classical_bits/structural.classical_bit_count: 571,051 vs 1,575, independently verified real).

metrics.definition: Peak number of live qubits used by the circuit (max qubit index + 1 observed across all operations).
metrics.source: STORED ONLY, as actually implemented -- see CORRECTION below
metrics.CORRECTION_from_code_audit_phase_2A: Earlier revisions of this file claimed this alias also resolves from computed structural analysis. Verified false by reading qch/query/metrics.py's _ALIASES table directly: the generic 'qubit_count' alias only ever reads a raw StructuralMetric literally named 'qubits' or a BenchmarkRun.peak_qubits field -- both V1-V5-manifest-only sources. hub.structures.analyze() (the computed path used by all Phase 1.5+ extraction) writes a metric named 'structural.qubit_count', a DIFFERENT literal metric_name the alias table never looks at. A query for 'qubit_count' against any version whose only qubit data came from structural extraction (i.e. every non-milestone version, ~776 of 781) will find NOTHING, even though 'structural.qubit_count' is present and correct for that same version. The NL planner and any caller MUST use 'structural.qubit_count' explicitly to reach computed data; 'qubit_count' unqualified only ever means the V1-V5 stored value.
metrics.comparable_across: Where both happen to be recorded for the same version (only ever true for V1/V4/V5 in the data seen so far), 'qubit_count' and 'structural.qubit_count' have been independently verified to agree exactly -- but they are not the same code path and not interchangeable as query metric names.

metrics.definition: Total number of operations (all kinds) in the built circuit.
metrics.source: STORED ONLY, as actually implemented -- see CORRECTION below
metrics.CORRECTION_from_code_audit_phase_2A: Same defect as 'qubit_count' above: the alias only reads a raw StructuralMetric literally named 'operations' (V1-V5 manifest). The computed path writes 'structural.operation_count', which this alias never reads. Use 'structural.operation_count' explicitly for computed data.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have the SAME one of these two metric names populated.

metrics.definition: Peak number of classical bits used (max classical-bit index + 1). NOT comparable to a 'total classical bits ever allocated' definition -- audited directly on V4 (571,051) vs V5 (1,575): both independently reproduced via real materialization+analysis, confirming this is a real, dramatic algorithmic change in classical-bit reuse strategy, not a units/definition inconsistency.
metrics.source: NOT AN ALIAS AT ALL, as actually implemented -- see CORRECTION below
metrics.availability: Neither form is reachable under this canonical name today.
metrics.CORRECTION_from_code_audit_phase_2A: This is worse than the two entries above: qch/query/metrics.py's _ALIASES table has NO entry at all for 'classical_bit_count' -- it is not a real, queryable metric name in the current implementation. The only two ACTUAL usable names are the raw StructuralMetric names 'classical_bits' (STORED, V1-V5 manifest only) and 'structural.classical_bit_count' (COMPUTED, Phase 1.5+ extraction). A planner or caller must use one of those two literal names; 'classical_bit_count' resolves to nothing for every version in the store.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two versions that both have the SAME one of the two real names populated ('classical_bits' or 'structural.classical_bit_count') -- but a large change reflects a real algorithmic difference, not noise; do not assume smoothness version-to-version.

metrics.definition: toffoli_count (average executed) * peak_qubits, per the ECDSA.Fail README's own scoring formula. Lower is better.
metrics.availability: Only the 5 frozen V1-V5 milestones (depends on the STORED, not computed, toffoli_count).

metrics.definition: Number of named classical registers declared.
metrics.source: STORED (V1-V5 manifest only; not currently computed by the structural parser)

metrics.definition: Requested by the Phase 1.5 spec as a candidate metric; deliberately NOT defined as a canonical metric here because 'gate' is ambiguous in this dataset (does it mean all 18 operation kinds, or only quantum gates excluding classical/control-flow pseudo-ops like push_condition/register?). operation_count and structural.toffoli_count are the two unambiguous quantities actually computed; a future 'gate_count' should be defined explicitly before being added here.
Circuit depth (longest dependency chain through the operation DAG).
metrics.availability: Never computed by any existing QCH pipeline for ECDSA.Fail data as of Phase 1.5 -- would require a new, not-yet-built dependency-chain analysis over the operation list.

metrics.definition: Count of operations acting on exactly two qubits (cx, cz, swap).
metrics.availability: Not currently computed as a named metric, though derivable from the same gate_counts histogram structural.toffoli_count already uses (cx+cz+swap) -- a straightforward future addition, not implemented in Phase 1.5 because no query in the initial workload required it yet.

metrics.definition: OFFICIAL peak qubits Q of a SUBMISSION as recorded by the ECDSA.Fail platform evaluator: the maximum qubit index used by any operation of the evaluated ops.bin, plus 1.
metrics.source: OFFICIAL (ECDSA.Fail platform API officialMetrics.qubits, imported from a content-addressed snapshot; provenance per value)
metrics.availability: Submissions whose official evaluation produced metrics (855 of 1003 in the first imported snapshot) -- including submissions with NO CircuitVersion.
metrics.relationship: Same formula as structural.qubit_count (and equal on all 25 versions QCH has analysed), but a SEPARATE measurement with separate provenance; never rewritten into it.
metrics.comparable_across: Any two submissions that both have an official evaluation.

metrics.definition: OFFICIAL T of a SUBMISSION: round(total EXECUTED Toffoli gates / tested shots) over up to 9,024 Fiat-Shamir-derived shots of the ECDSA.Fail evaluator, recorded only when every validity check passed.
metrics.source: OFFICIAL (ECDSA.Fail platform API officialMetrics.toffoli, imported from a content-addressed snapshot; provenance per value)
metrics.availability: Submissions whose official evaluation produced metrics (855 of 1003 in the first imported snapshot).
metrics.NOT_an_alias_of: structural.toffoli_count (a STATIC gate count of ops.bin; 5.2-6.3% higher on all 25 comparable versions). For V1-V5 the benchmark-run toffoli_count holds the SAME official value (same fact, older provenance).
metrics.comparable_across: Any two submissions that both have an official evaluation.

metrics.definition: OFFICIAL score of a SUBMISSION: evaluation.avg_executed_toffoli * evaluation.peak_qubits, as recorded by the ECDSA.Fail platform (verified equal to Q*T on every imported record). Lower is better.
metrics.source: OFFICIAL (ECDSA.Fail platform API officialScore, imported from a content-addressed snapshot; provenance per value)
metrics.availability: Submissions whose official evaluation produced metrics (855 of 1003 in the first imported snapshot).
metrics.relationship: For V1-V5 the benchmark-run score holds the SAME official value (same fact, older provenance).
metrics.comparable_across: Any two submissions that both have an official evaluation.

submission_field_notes: Fields of list_submissions records (QCH Phase 2D.5). lifecycle_status is QCH's Git-derived SUBMITTED/VALIDATED/PROMOTED; platform.status is the official accepted/rejected/failed/cancelled -- separate vocabularies, never mapped onto each other. evaluation.passed is DERIVED (true iff official metrics exist), not a source field.
known_limitations: Contributors are platform ACCOUNTS identified by handle or stable account key (QCH Phase 2D.6); no real/person names are known, so a person's name is never resolved or guessed. Declared co-authors are unverified strings, never linked to an account. A CircuitVersion's contributor is derived through its Submission.

evaluation.* and platform.* are SUBMISSION facts from imported official-API snapshots (not live); list_version records never contain them. Bare 'score'/'Toffoli'/'qubits' keep their pre-0.6.0 grounding; say 'official'/'evaluation' (or 'peak qubits', 'average executed Toffoli') to ground the official evaluation metrics.

Structural metrics require the post-2026-06-22 zstd 'QECCOPSZ' ops.bin wire format; earlier commits (roughly V1-V3 era and before) are materializable but not structurally analyzable by the current parser.
Only 5 of 781 versions have STORED benchmark toffoli_count/score data; structural.toffoli_count is COMPUTED-only and is a different quantity.

Materialization requires a real cargo build per version (~30-200+ seconds observed), so bulk structural-metric coverage grows only as fast as pipeline runs are actually executed -- see the Phase 1.5 coverage report for exactly how many versions have been processed as of this file's last regeneration.
version_label is set only for the 5 frozen milestones; every other version must be addressed by version_id or external_version_key.
